title: Midnight release oversight journal
summary: Notes and action items from the on-call release team that managed the 2026-03-10 midnight release window. Document captures observed anomalies during canary ramp, mitigation steps, decisions for roll-forwards/rollbacks, and tasks to harden the next overnight push.
notes:
Context: We scheduled a twilight canary for dedicated clusters (eu-west-1) to land kernel selection changes and a small topology optimizer (PR 582). Window 00:30-03:00 UTC. Primary goal: validate p95 latency improvements against 1k req/sec simulated traffic while preserving tail error rate <0.5%.

Timeline (concise):
- 00:15: Pre-flight check: infra autoscale targets verified, kv-cache flush script reviewed (todo: add checksum), canary cohort size = 8 pods.
- 00:30: Canary started. Synthetic load ramp to 200 rps. Initial p95 dropped ~7% vs baseline. Good. No errors.
- 00:48: Observed intermittent 502 spikes on two canary pods coincident with long GC pause in the host VM (host vm metrics show CPU steal). Error rate for the cohort jumped to 1.2%.
- 00:52: Follow-up: shifted canary traffic away from affected hosts to standby pods; rolled a host-level remedial kernel flag bump (temp). 502s stopped after 6 minutes. Kept canary paused for 12m of stable signal.
- 01:10: Resumed ramp to 600 rps. p95 stable. Noted a small memory growth trend on coordinator process in one pod (approx +140MB over 25m). Left under watch.
- 01:42: Reached target 1k rps. p95 stable but p99 had a small spike (from 420ms -> 680ms) when an eviction of KV cache happened on one pod due to memory pressure. That pod recovered after cache warm-up ~90s.
- 01:48: Decision point: proceed or abort. Tradeoff: latency improvement across 90% of requests vs transient p99 spikes and 2 brief 502 bursts earlier. Decided to proceed with a staged rollout to 40% of dedicated cluster capacity with auto-fallback to previous kernel selection (policy set). Rollout initiated.
- 02:20: At 40% rollout, an unrelated downstream service (reranker-v2) reported increased 429 throttles which caused request queuing in the gateway and subsequent timeout cascades for a small fraction (~0.07% of global traffic). Rolled back traffic slice from 40% -> 25% and enacted backpressure to reranker-v2.
- 02:45: After coordination with platform team, reranker throttle windows increased, queue drains, global errors normalized. Post-rollback telemetry acceptable.
- 03:00: End of window. Final decision: continue staged rollout with additional mitigations (see action items).

Notes-to-self / unresolved items:
- Need a more deterministic host health check for canary placement (current tie to vm-metrics is noisy during noisy neighbors).
- KV-cache eviction pattern: investigate allocator threshold vs pod memory requests; consider bumping requests for coordinator processes by +200MB on canary cohorts.
- Add a fail-fast detector that quarantines pods with repeated 502s in <10m and removes them from canary without manual intervention.
- Confirm whether the kernel flag bump had any side-effects on quantized model paths (Maya to validate against offline eval-set).

Observability snippets (copied metrics):
- Canary cohort error rate peak: 1.25% (00:48) -> baseline target <0.5%
- P95 baseline: 210ms, canary p95: 195ms at 1k rps
- P99 baseline: 420ms, saw max 680ms (01:42) during KV eviction
- Avg tokens/sec per GPU: baseline 18.7k -> canary 19.8k (measured on 4xA100 equivalent hosts)

Stakeholder messages (sent during window):
- Slack #release-ops: "canary started 00:30 UTC; small 502 spike 00:48 on 2 hosts, shifting off those hosts. Watching p99 for KV evictions. Will update 01:00."
- PagerDuty rotation: notified second on-call (Leo) at 00:50 when 502 spike exceeded threshold.

Good catches and wins:
- Autoscale ramp handled 1k rps gracefully after brief rebalancing; no sustained saturation observed on host GPU metrics.
- Rollback policy and traffic-slice primitives worked as expected; we reverted traffic slices within 6 minutes when reranker throttling was detected.

Risks and mitigations for next overnight: 
- Risk: Noisy neighbor causing host GC/steal -> Mitigation: Reserve dedicated host pool for canaries or enforce stricter anti-affinity in scheduler.
- Risk: KV eviction causing p99 blips -> Mitigation: increase pod memory request for coordinator; add a cache pre-warm step in rollout.
- Risk: Downstream service throttles not surfaced until cascade -> Mitigation: add early throttling signal from common reranker layer to release traffic sooner.

Decision log: 
- 01:48 Proceed with staged rollout to 40% + policy fallback (decision owner: Asha).
- 02:20 Partial rollback to 25% to give reranker breathing room (decision owner: Jordan).
- 03:00 Keep staged rollout but pause expansion until cache/host fixes applied (decision owner: Release-Lead rotation).
